in_hebrew.name: עָלָה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: This Hebrew name can be derived from the root 'alah' which means 'to go up, ascend, or rise high'. It can refer to a person of high status or a place of great height. In the Bible, the name is used to describe various things, such as mountains, cities, and people who are exalted or lifted up in some way.

in_greek.name: ὕψιστος
in_greek.long_meaning: The Greek name ὕψιστος comes from the root 'ὕψις' which means 'height, highness, or altitude'. It is used in the Bible to describe God as the most high or supreme being. It can also refer to someone or something that is of the highest rank or status.

in_latin.name: Altissimus
in_latin.long_meaning: The Latin name Altissimus is derived from the same root as the Greek name ὕψιστος. It means 'most high' or 'highest'. In the Bible, it is used to describe God as the highest being and to refer to those who hold the highest positions or ranks.
